plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single isometric line drawing of a rectangular block subdivided into unit cells, drawn entirely in salmon-red strokes on white. The block reads as a stack of small cubes: the front face is ruled into a four-by-four arrangement of square cells, and the visible top and right-hand faces are ruled into matching grids receding from the viewer, so an interior lattice is implied throughout. Three black dimension bars with serif end caps mark the extents. A vertical bar along the left edge is labeled H, a bar beneath the lower-left edge is labeled W, and a bar beneath the lower-right edge, receding away from the viewer, is labeled C. Near the back of the top face one cell is drawn displaced from the surface, isolating a single unit cube, and a white square panel with a thin black border and a soft drop shadow floats just above it carrying the boldface letter X. Ruling the volume into addressable cells rather than drawing a smooth solid keeps every entry individually locatable by its three coordinates. The picture gives a concrete spatial reading of a three-axis tensor whose dimensions are channels, height, and width, the shape used to hold a color image.

elements: 4x4x4 lattice of unit cube cells forming the tensor volume (64 addressable cells)
outer wireframe edges of the whole block in salmon-red
interior grid ruling on the three visible faces (front 4x4, top 4x4, right 4x4) implying the full lattice
vertical black dimension bar with serif end caps on the left edge labeled H
black dimension bar with serif end caps beneath the lower-left receding edge labeled W
black dimension bar with serif end caps beneath the lower-right receding edge labeled C
one isolated unit cube displaced outward from the back-top surface (the X cell)
white square panel with thin black border and soft drop shadow floating above the X cell carrying boldface letter X
highlighted H-by-W channel sheet (one depth slice) that lights up as the slider moves
on-demand index label showing (c, h, w) for a hovered cell

interactions.label: Channel c
interactions.teaches: Sweeping c highlights one full H-by-W sheet at a single depth position, showing that a color image tensor is a stack of aligned spatial maps — one per channel — rather than one flat picture
Hovering any small cube lifts it and reveals its (c, h, w) index, tying one stored scalar value to its exact location inside the three-axis volume
Rotating the block confirms the three independent axes (H vertical, W and C receding) and that every interior cell is reachable by a unique triple of coordinates

demo_steps.title: Channel 0 (front sheet)
demo_steps.narration: The c=0 sheet at the front of the volume is highlighted as a full 4x4 H-by-W plane. This is the first spatial map stored in the tensor.

demo_steps.title: Channel 1
demo_steps.narration: The highlight steps one unit deeper along C to c=1. The same H-by-W layout repeats at a new depth — a second aligned spatial map.

demo_steps.title: Channel 3 (back sheet)
demo_steps.narration: At c=3 the highlighted sheet sits at the back of the block. Four stacked sheets along C together form the complete 4x4x4 image tensor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World space: each unit cell is 1x1x1; the volume is 4 (W) x 4 (H) x 4 (C). Axis mapping for the standard isometric pose: +Y = H (vertical, matches the left H bar), +X = C (recedes to screen lower-right, matches the C bar), +Z = W (recedes to screen lower-left, matches the W bar). So a channel sheet at fixed c is the H-by-W plane spanning Y in [0,4], Z in [0,4] at X = c..c+1. Stroke color salmon-red #f4726b for all lattice edges; highlighted sheet edges/faces use a stronger red #e23b2e with ~0.18 face opacity; the X/isolated cell and any hovered cell lift ~0.6 units outward along its face normal and show a white #ffffff panel with black #000000 border and bold 'X' or the (c,h,w) text. Dimension bars and H/W/C labels are black #000000 with serif end caps, placed just outside the corresponding block edges. Block centered near origin so it spans roughly X in [0,4], Y in [0,4], Z in [0,4]; recenter to [-2,2] on each axis for framing.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the lattice as 64 transparent BoxGeometry cells (opacity ~0.04 fill) each with an EdgesGeometry LineSegments in salmon-red so every cell is individually hoverable via raycasting; on hover, raise that cell's group position along its outward normal and swap its label sprite to '(c, h, w)'. For the channel slider, keep a separate highlighted sheet mesh (4x4 grid of edges plus a translucent plane) that is repositioned to X = c on each change rather than rebuilding. Use a single isometric camera (no perspective vanishing) to match the source line-drawing look; disable shadows except a soft sprite shadow under the floating X panel. Throttle raycast to pointermove.

authoredContext:
This example shows the basic concept of working with tensors and batches
for one-dimensional data, but, in vision, most of the time we will be
working with higher-dimensional tensors. For image data we typically use
four-dimensional tensors: batch $\times$ channels $\times$ height
$\times$ width; for videos we may use five-dimensional tensors: batch
$\times$ channels $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ time.
Three-dimensional (3D) scans have an additional depth spatial
dimension; videos of 3D data could therefore be represented by
six-dimensional tensors. As you can see, thinking in terms of
two-dimensional matrices is not quite sufficient. Instead, you should be
imagining data processing as operating on $N$-dimensional tensors,
sliced and diced in different ways. As a step in this direction, you may
find it useful to visualize tensors in 3D, as shown in
the figure.

A 3D tensor that could represent an $C \times H \times W$ color image.

discrepancies: A semi-transparent red channel sheet with grid lines is visible by default on the left face, which does not appear in the source figure
Grid lines in the generated figure are noticeably thinner than the thick salmon-colored lines in the source
The source figure shows only wireframe edges with no filled faces; the generated figure adds faint filled boxes (opacity 0.04) that slightly alter the clean wireframe appearance
evaluation.notes: The 4×4×4 tensor grid, dimension bars (H, W, C), and X element panel are all correctly represented in an axonometric view matching the source; the main deviation is the channel sheet highlight visible by default which is an interactive enhancement not present in the source but pedagogically useful.
action_items: Consider making the channel sheet invisible by default (or at very low opacity) so the initial view more closely matches the pure wireframe source figure
Increase the line width of the grid edges to better match the thick salmon lines in the source figure
